title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the end of a sentence that starts on the previous page (p.26 of the internal numbering), followed by an unfinished paragraph that begins only with "Quand".

Setting from the previous page. P_n is an n-element combinatorial object (plausibly an n-gon, or n cyclically ordered points) with symmetry group D_{P_n}, likely dihedral. Σ_{P_n} is a complex space identified with a projective space P(V_{P̃_{2n}})(C), where V_{P̃_{2n}} is a vector space attached to a degree-2 covering P̃_{2n} → P_n. Σ*_{P_n} ⊂ Σ_{P_n} is an open part, presumably the complement of a discriminant or degenerate locus.

The bundle. D_{P_n} acts on Σ_{P_n} and on a degree-1 invertible sheaf O(1). PΣ_{P_n} is the principal C*-bundle of O(1) (the punctured tautological line bundle, i.e. essentially V minus 0, up to taking the dual). D_{P_n} does not act naturally on this bundle; the action is defined only up to scalars, a projective-representation or central-extension obstruction. Once the double cover P̃_{2n} is chosen, the group D_{P̃_{2n}} (an extension of D_{P_n} by Z/2) does act. PΣ*_{P_n} is the restriction of this bundle over Σ*_{P_n}.

What this page states. Grothendieck is interested in:
- the fundamental groupoid of PΣ*_{P_n}, with the action of D_{P̃_{2n}} on it;
- in particular, the "groupe fondamental mixte". In modern terms this is the orbifold or equivariant fundamental group of the quotient stack [PΣ* / D̃]: an extension 1 → π1(PΣ*) → Π → D̃ → 1.
- He then refines the group to D_{P̃_{2n}} × {1,τ}. Here τ is presumably complex conjugation, an antiholomorphic involution coming from the real structure. The resulting mixed group also maps onto Gal(C/R), in the spirit of his anabelian and Teichmüller-tower program, where the arithmetic or real Galois action is built into the fundamental group.

The new paragraph "Quand ..." breaks off immediately. The next page is empty apart from its page number, 101.

Purpose. These are equivariant, C*-bundle-enhanced (braid-type) fundamental groups of configuration-like spaces with dihedral symmetry. They are natural ingredients of the Teichmüller tower in genus 0, together with the action of complex conjugation.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page is only the end of a sentence plus an unfinished one. Whether D_{P̃_{2n}} is a direct product with {1,τ} or should instead be a semidirect product depends on τ commuting with the D-action. That is plausible for a combinatorially defined action, but it is not checked here.
